answer: Each identity files a shale slab in a mirror registry: an assayer stamps a sable seal binding it to the identity key and locks a 70-credit bond. A duplicate filing is caught by the mirror check and both bonds burn. Fees rise per filing: first 36 credits, thousandth 8,028, so 1,000 fakes pay 4,032,000 and lock 70,000 against a 40,000 pool. A rented slab fails, its sable seal naming another key. An honest agent files once for 36 and keeps its bond.
